items.title: Chemists develop AI tool to convert human ingenuity into life-enhancing enzymes
items.excerpt: Vanderbilt's MutexaGPT uses LLM agents to turn plain-language, intuition-based enzyme requests into physics-based enzyme models and proposed mutations (Nature Computational Science).

items.title: New AI tool helps scientists identify bacteria hidden in soil
items.excerpt: BBERT, a DNA language model, classifies 100-base soil-DNA fragments as bacterial (~90% accuracy) and finds reading frames (~96%) without reference databases, cutting genome reconstruction from ~66 to 25 hours (Nucleic Acids Research).

items.title: AI used to identify new human cell-surface proteins missing from major databases
items.excerpt: A Claude Sonnet 4.6-based literature agent judged whether proteins sit on human cell surfaces with 95.7% accuracy (vs ~90% for UniProt) and flagged 1,108 surface proteins absent from all five major databases (bioRxiv).

items.title: AI often passes for human, but asking follow-up questions can trip it up
items.excerpt: In 72,000+ judgments of output from 636 people and 37 AI models across six language and vision tasks, judges often mistook AI for human, but live follow-up questioning exposed chatbots better as conversations grew longer (Nature Human Behaviour).

items.title: AIs fail to reliably detect AIs in reverse Turing tests
items.excerpt: Seven LLMs acting as interrogators in 238 reverse Turing tests identified only 3 of 98 AI respondents while correctly flagging 123 of 140 humans (Computers in Human Behavior Reports).

items.title: AI framework cuts computing use by two-thirds while more than tripling success in virtual tasks
items.excerpt: SKKU's SAG lets an agent gauge its own uncertainty and request feedback only when worth it, cutting compute to about a third and raising virtual-task success from 24.6% to 78.3%; companion VAN-Flow RL filters lucky successes (NeurIPS 2026).

items.title: People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
items.excerpt: Researchers used AI to analyze nearly 150,000 Reddit posts about unapproved retatrutide, surfacing symptom reports (increased appetite, sleep disturbances, elevated heart rate) that differ from clinical-trial results.

items.title: AI detects 'invisible' signs of pancreatic cancer years before diagnosis
items.excerpt: The REDMOD AI model spotted subtle pancreatic tissue changes an average of 475 days before diagnosis and was nearly twice as sensitive as experienced radiologists (Gut).

items.title: 10 minutes is all it takes for AI assistance to erode your motivation, study shows
items.excerpt: In problem-solving experiments, people who used AI to get answers were more likely to give up and fail once the help was removed than people who never used AI.

items.title: Could AI ever build itself? Scientists map the road to the 'last AI built by humans'
items.excerpt: Researchers examine whether recursive self-improvement, AI systems automating AI research, is viable as a way to tame the soaring cost of developing frontier models.

items.title: Space outposts beyond the Moon may rely on planetary AI
items.excerpt: Ohio State's LUMINA builds on lunar vision-language model LLaVA-LE to plan multistep analyses, rank candidate lunar landing sites and explain its evidence (presented at AAS DPS 58).

items.title: To detect deepfake videos, researchers turn to the physics of light
items.excerpt: An optical deepfake-detection technique claims 97.8% accuracy while using less energy than digital neural networks with similar performance.

items.title: Why teaching AI about symmetry could make prenatal diagnosis more reliable
items.excerpt: MIT's E(3)-Pose, a symmetry-aware AI model, helps capture high-resolution fetal head images to improve early detection of developmental anomalies.

items.title: Empowering frontline maternal care with AI-assisted ultrasound
items.excerpt: In a 385-participant prospective study in Chicago and Nairobi, Google's blind-sweep ultrasound model estimated gestational age on mobile devices with novice operators (MAE 4.18 days vs 4.48 for expert sonographers).

items.title: Bringing foundational models to the front lines of TB screening
items.excerpt: Google's chest X-ray TB algorithms, certified via Nexus AI, now run in ~40 facilities in six countries, cutting turnaround from weeks to under 45 seconds; open MedSigLIP/MedGemma models run offline.

items.title: An exclusive conversation with the developer of REA, the viral AI reverse engineering tool
items.excerpt: REA, an AI tool that reverse engineers closed software in printers, smart TVs and cars; its pseudonymous creator explains why everyone should get a look inside.
